name: simulate-ordinary-withdrawal-boundary
why: Measured reach for the exact-cent annual ordinary-withdrawal transaction boundary extracted from simulatePlan. The helper entry pins the complete executable helper body: Plan-number snapshots, exact-cent execution, fact-removal retries, aggregate totals, and positional closing writes. The paired callsite entry pins complete caller consumption. Four dedicated block-M members run in all four equivalence modes and discriminate normal mixed-source execution, aggregate Plan-boundary failure, unrepresentable closing balance, and both missing opening and unrepresentable closing taxable-basis evidence.

taxable source and tax-unit selection
entries.note: The null-tax-unit ternary on lines 139-141 is excluded: validated annual simulation constructs a tax unit whenever individually owned taxable evidence can be published, while focused helper tests cover the structural null input. Lines 153-159 are the multiline comparator operands; block M reaches deterministic sorting with distinct ids, and their exclusion avoids misreporting formatting branches as cold production statements.

entries.note: Block M reaches valid taxable evidence, invalid opening-basis omission, ordinary person evidence, and the legacy aggregate no-person arm. V8 reports the non-member owner and QCD-donor operands as cold sub-line regions: the annual call gives this helper ordinary/legacy execution requests, while owner-membership failure is a supported defensive structural input covered by helper tests.

entries.note: Block M reaches normal execution, every nonzero total class, aggregate Plan-boundary failure, unrepresentable closing balance, unrepresentable closing basis, and both opening-balance and taxable-basis filtering on retry.

readingTheCounts: A member count proves that at least one line in the named range executed. The reach command additionally fails on any cold executable whole line inside a reached range. JavaScript line coverage cannot distinguish every ternary, nullish, optional-chain, or compound-condition operand sharing one physical line, so the report's cold sub-line regions and focused helper/delegation tests must be read alongside this differential proof.
